import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    shipments = inputs["shipments"].copy()
    carrier_rates = inputs["carrier_rates"].copy()
    
    # Merge shipments with carrier_rates on carrier_id (creates many-to-many)
    merged = shipments.merge(
        carrier_rates,
        on="carrier_id",
        how="left"
    )
    
    # For each shipment_id, we need to select the best matching rate
    # Sort by effective_date DESC, then rate_id DESC
    # Keep only the first per shipment_id
    
    # First, sort the entire merged dataframe by the resolution criteria
    merged = merged.sort_values(
        by=["shipment_id", "effective_date", "rate_id"],
        ascending=[True, False, False],
        na_position="last"
    )
    
    # Drop duplicates keeping the first occurrence per shipment_id
    # This ensures we keep the row with the highest effective_date and rate_id
    resolved = merged.drop_duplicates(subset=["shipment_id"], keep="first")
    
    # Reset index to clean up
    resolved = resolved.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Fill in defaults for missed lookups
    resolved["rate_per_kg"] = resolved["rate_per_kg"].fillna(0.0)
    resolved["service_tier"] = resolved["service_tier"].fillna("NONE")
    
    # Compute freight_cost
    resolved["freight_cost"] = resolved["weight_kg"] * resolved["rate_per_kg"]
    
    # Select and order output columns
    output_columns = ["shipment_id", "carrier_id", "service_tier", "weight_kg", "rate_per_kg", "freight_cost"]
    result = resolved[output_columns].copy()
    
    return {"shipment_costs": result}
